description: IGNIS Innovators is a Windsor-based NASA Space Apps team developing IGNIS Atlas — FireTruth, a scientific web application that harmonizes NASA MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire observations. Our project explores historical burning activity, sensor differences, and evidence-based trend analysis. We combine software development, data science, remote sensing, and interactive visualization to make Earth observation data more understandable, reproducible, and useful.
summary:
IGNIS Atlas — FireTruth is an interactive research platform that helps scientists compare NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire observations without confusing differences between satellite sensors with changes in wildfire activity.

MODIS (~1 km) and VIIRS (~375 m) differ in spatial resolution, sensitivity, and observation conditions, making raw hotspot counts misleading when compared directly.

Using authentic NASA FIRMS observations, FireTruth applies confidence filtering, a shared 25 km equal-area grid, and active cell-day aggregation. It evaluates three calibration approaches using chronological training and holdout periods.

Our key finding reveals that calibration does not automatically transfer between regions. In Oregon/Washington, California-trained seasonal calibration produced an RMSE of 400.95, worse than the uncorrected baseline of 389.21. Locally trained calibration reduced RMSE to 132.75.

These values measure MODIS–VIIRS agreement, not independent fire-detection accuracy. FireTruth combines interactive maps, scientific validation, reproducibility records, and evidence checks to help researchers identify reliable comparisons and avoid unsupported conclusions.
details:
The Problem

NASA's MODIS and VIIRS satellites provide valuable active-fire observations, but their hotspot detections are not directly interchangeable. Differences in spatial resolution, detection sensitivity, orbital sampling, and observation conditions can produce misleading apparent changes in fire activity.

Our Solution

IGNIS Atlas — FireTruth is an interactive research platform that harmonizes MODIS and VIIRS observations into a shared analytical framework. It helps users understand where the sensors agree, where they disagree, and when calibration results cannot be trusted without additional evidence.

How It Works

The platform uses authentic NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS standard-processing observations.

Observations undergo confidence filtering and are mapped to a common 25 km authalic sinusoidal equal-area grid. Detections are deduplicated by sensor, grid cell, and UTC day, producing comparable active cell-day measurements.

Three approaches are evaluated:

  • B0: Uncorrected baseline.
  • B1: Global scalar calibration.
  • B2: Seasonally regularized calibration.

Chronological training and holdout periods help prevent evaluation leakage.

Scientific Validation

California, 2018–2022

Training: January 2018–June 2020.
Holdout: July 2020–December 2022.

Held-out MODIS–VIIRS agreement RMSE:

  • B0: 694.74
  • B1: 478.58
  • B2: 464.29

Oregon/Washington Cross-Region Transfer

Held-out RMSE:

  • B0: 389.21
  • California zero-shot B1: 395.50
  • California zero-shot B2: 400.95
  • Destination-local B1: 194.75
  • Destination-local B2: 132.75

The central finding is that California-trained calibration did not automatically transfer to Oregon/Washington. The zero-shot seasonal calibration performed worse than the uncorrected baseline, while destination-local calibration improved agreement.

This demonstrates why region-specific validation matters.

Interactive Features

FireTruth provides ten research views and a six-chapter Guided Scientific Story. Features include:

  • Fire Explorer with geographic comparisons.
  • Harmonization Lab for calibration evaluation.
  • Cross-Region Transfer Lab.
  • California 2020 Case Study.
  • Evidence Resolver with six scientific evidence checks.
  • Scientific Dossier documenting methodology, provenance, and limitations.

Technology

The application uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Python, scientific data-processing scripts, automated tests, GitHub, and Vercel.

The workflow incorporates NASA FIRMS observations, geospatial aggregation, chronological validation, scientific artifacts, and interactive visualizations.

Creativity and Impact

FireTruth goes beyond displaying wildfire hotspots. It makes sensor differences visible, evaluates calibration transfer, and explicitly identifies when the available evidence does not support a confident conclusion.

Potential users include Earth-observation researchers, wildfire analysts, environmental monitoring teams, educators, and developers of geospatial tools.

Scientific Limitations

VIIRS is a comparison sensor, not independent ground truth. RMSE measures agreement between MODIS and VIIRS, not wildfire-detection accuracy.

Active cell-days do not represent individual fires, burned area, or complete fire perimeters.

CAL FIRE/FRAP final fire perimeters provide independent contextual evidence, not daily detection labels.

FireTruth is a research demonstrator, not an operational wildfire-warning or forecasting system.

Future Development

Future improvements include additional geographic validation, independent reference datasets, observation-completeness analysis, and broader uncertainty evaluation.
